title: 4-round AES-192: 15-parameter conditional distinguisher

target.description: 4 inner AES rounds without initial whitening, including MixColumns in every round; fixed keys and explicitly conditioned input structures.

setting.key_relation: Fixed standard AES key schedule; component derivations treat its round-key bytes as constants, not as a related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: Every fixed AES key; probability is over passive-context selection, not over a weak-key subset.
setting.plaintext_model: Choose the fifteen passive plaintext bytes independently and uniformly once; keep them fixed while the active byte takes all 256 values.
assumptions: The displayed bound uses a uniformly random passive context and complete membership in the corrected 15-byte difference-function family.
The2^-72 number is a qualifying-parameter event, not a stated distinguishing advantage or complete recovery rate.
setting.reference_model: A uniformly random128-bit permutation under the same classical chosen-plaintext interface.

success.description: Advantage lower bound for COMPLETE corrected 15-byte difference-family membership on one 256-query structure. Fifteen passive bytes are independently uniform before the structure and fixed across it; the key is arbitrary and fixed. The actual AES dependency map gives nine independent byte constraints on twelve uniform external bytes, so the sufficient parameter event has probability exactly 2^-72 without uniform ci or key assumptions. The fourth-round output-key byte cancels, leaving at most2^120 anchored255-byte difference vectors. Finite-permutation sampling without replacement gives the displayed ideal false-alarm upper bound. Use the corrected coefficient1 in Equation9, obtained by substituting Equation7 into correct Equations3–6 and12, not the literal printed table. This is a derived tiny-advantage bound, not the source 50% seven-round key-recovery rate. Standalone computation costs remain unreported; the printed-equation discrepancy and historical local component are retained.

review.scope: Read all 13 DTCB09 PDF pages. Reconstruct corrected 15-byte difference-family membership and prove Equation7 event probability exactly 2^-72 for every fixed key under uniform passive-context selection using three disjoint rank 3 affine systems. Prove255-coordinate anchored finite-permutation false acceptance at the existing256-query budget. Clarify only input-randomness/key-population/assumption wording; native resources, round boundary, local component, source conflict and audit gates retained. Targeted success proof, not a new full-paper or forward audit.

evidence.interpretation: Supersedes only the absence of a complete statistical bound and clarifies its passive-context randomness. Under uniform passive plaintext selection the 12 external first-round S-box bytes are jointly uniform; Equation7 gives three disjoint rank 3 affine systems, so its sufficient event has exact probability2^-72 for every fixed key, without assuming 20 independent constants. Complete corrected 15-byte family membership accepts on that event. Literal Equation9 uses coefficient3 where substitution in Equation4 requires1; the existing source discrepancy remains and the guarantee does not certify the unmodified printed table.

evidence.locator: PDF6–7/printed149–150 Equations12–13 and normalized difference f(i)+f(0); reviewer finite-permutation derivation2026-11-07.
evidence.interpretation: Normalize all 256 output bytes by the first, yielding255 differences and at most2^120 family vectors. Condition on the first full ideal output; at step i=1,...,255 each required output byte has at most2^120 eligible blocks among 2^128-i remaining blocks. The union bound gives beta=2^120*product_{i=1}^{255}2^120/(2^128-i), hence advantage at least2^-72-beta. This is a derived bound for the explicit256-query corrected-family test, not author-printed success, iid bytes, the 32-difference wrong-key estimate or the later50% recovery rate. Unknown standalone costs remain unknown.
